info.title: SaaSFlow Public API
info.description:
REST API for SaaSFlow, the finance cockpit for SaaS companies: bank accounts and transactions, customers, vendors, subscriptions and MRR, planned transactions, files, reports and pre-aggregated analytics (data slices).

Every route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is a SaaSFlow API key (`sf_…`, created in Settings → Company settings → API keys) or an OAuth 2.1 access token. Everything except `/companies` itself is scoped under `/companies/{companyId}/…`. Each operation lists the permission an API key needs (`x-saasflow-permissions`) and the OAuth scope a third-party app must hold.

Documentation: https://docs.saasflow.com/developers · MCP server: https://api.saasflow.com/mcp · Support: support@saasflow.com

bearerAuth.description: A SaaSFlow API key (`sf_…`) or a signed-in user session token. API keys are scoped to one company and to the permission set chosen when the key was created.

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.1 authorization code with PKCE for third-party apps and hosted MCP clients. Dynamic client registration is supported. Discovery: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`.

scopes.saasflow:read: Read data in every company the granting user can access.
scopes.saasflow:write: Create, update and delete data in every company the granting user can access. Implies saasflow:read.
scopes.saasflow:admin: Change company settings and manage integrations in every company where the granting user may. Never members, roles or API keys.
scopes.saasflow:create_companies: Create companies for the granting user, who accepted the Terms of Service and the data processing agreement on their behalf when granting it.

get.description: List the companies the authenticated caller can reach, with their `role` in each and the effective `permissions`. Start here when you do not have a `companyId`: every other endpoint is scoped to one company. A `permissions` of null means the role preset applies rather than an explicit allowlist. An API key scoped to a single company sees only that one.

200.description: List of companies the user has access to

name.description: The name of the company.

baseCurrency.description: The base currency for the company.

domain.description: The company's website domain, such as example.com. Null when not set.

customLogoPath.description: Path of the logo uploaded in the company settings, relative to the public assets host. Null when the company shows the logo of its website domain.

lastOverallUpdatedTime.description: When any data within the company was last updated.

dataStartDate.description: The company-wide data start date. Imports skip transactions dated before it. Null means no start date is set.

valuationCategory.description: Self-declared company category used by the valuation estimate. Null means traditional B2B SaaS.

valuationLens.description: Which comparable set the valuation estimate prices against. Null means fundraising.

items.description: A granular permission in the form `<resource>:<action>`. Stored on companiesUsers and companiesApiKeys. When a grant has `permissions: null` it means unrestricted (legacy behavior derived from role).

post.description: Create a company for the person you act for, with them as its owner. A regular company (`type` `owned`, the default) starts a 14-day trial. A sandbox (`type` `sandbox`) is for demos and testing: it has no trial, can be filled with sample data (`addSampleData`), and is deleted automatically after 14 days. Only an OAuth connection the person allowed to create companies can call this: on that consent screen they accepted the Terms of Service and the data processing agreement on behalf of the companies it creates. API keys cannot. A 403 with `code` `legal_acceptance_required` means the connection was granted without that, or the documents changed since: ask the person to reconnect SaaSFlow and allow "Create companies for you", or to create the company at the returned `url`. Calling again with the same name, currency and type within 10 minutes returns the company already created (200) instead of a duplicate. Sample data is filled in the background: follow it in `background_tasks_list` before reading numbers. Next steps: connect an integration (`integrations_connect_link`) or import data.

baseCurrency.description: The currency every report is converted into. Pick the one the company does its books in.

domain.description: The company's website, used for its logo. Dropped if it is not a domain.

type.description: `owned` is a real company on a 14-day trial. `sandbox` is a test company without a trial, deleted automatically after 14 days.

addSampleData.description: Fill the sandbox with sample accounts, customers, subscriptions, transactions and planned transactions. Only for `type` `sandbox`.

200.description: The company this connection created with that name moments ago

201.description: Created; `url` opens it in the app

get.description: Retrieve one company with its settings and its member list. `baseCurrency` is the currency every cross-currency figure is converted into, so read it before interpreting any aggregate amount. Returns 404 if the company does not exist or the caller has no access to it.

put.description: Update company settings. Only the fields you send change. Changing `baseCurrency` restates every converted figure in the app, including historical ones, so it is not a cosmetic setting. `plShowPlanningPercentageForPastMonths` and `plShowAllCategories` control how the P&L is rendered, and the valuation fields drive the valuation estimate.

get.description: List the people with an actual membership in a company, with their role and when they were last seen. `id` and `userId` both carry the SaaSFlow user id, which is what the role and remove endpoints expect. A null `lastSeenTime` means they have never opened the app. Pending invitations are not memberships and do not appear here, so someone who was invited but never accepted is missing from this list rather than showing up inactive.

200.description: List of users in the company

put.description: Upload the company's logo. It replaces the logo SaaSFlow takes from the website `domain` wherever the company is shown, until you delete it again. Send a PNG of at most 1024×1024 pixels and 512 KB as base64 in `imageBase64`; a square image of 256×256 pixels works best. Returns the updated company, whose `customLogoPath` points at the new image.

put.description: Change a member's role, and optionally their explicit permissions. Leave `permissions` out to keep whatever they have, send an array to pin an exact allowlist, or send null to drop back to the role's preset. Nobody can edit their own membership through this endpoint (403), which is what stops an owner locking themselves out.

role.description: The role assigned to a user within the system. Owner = full access incl. company settings, billing, and user management; editor = read/write on data; viewer = read-only. The role is also used as the default permission preset and as a non-permission marker (e.g. notifications are sent to all owners). For granular API access control, see PermissionSchema.

items.description: A granular permission in the form `<resource>:<action>`. Stored on companiesUsers and companiesApiKeys. When a grant has `permissions: null` it means unrestricted (legacy behavior derived from role).

403.description: Cannot edit own membership

delete.description: Remove someone from a company. Their user account survives, they just lose access to this company, and the data they created stays. Removing yourself is refused with 403.

403.description: Cannot remove self

get.description: List a company's account groups. Groups are the sections bank accounts are filed under (for example "Operating" or "Savings"). Archived groups are included, so filter on `archived` if you only want the active ones. Results come back unsorted; sort by `order` ascending to match the order the app shows.

name.description: The name of the account group.

archived.description: Flag indicating if the account group is archived.

order.description: A number used for ordering account groups in the UI.

post.description: Create an account group. `order` is required and sets the position in the list; pass a number higher than every existing group to append at the end. Assign accounts to the new group with `PUT /accounts/{accountId}/change_group`.

name.description: The name of the account group.

archived.description: Flag indicating if the account group is archived.

order.description: A number used for ordering account groups in the UI.

put.description: Set the display order of account groups. Pass every group id in the order you want them shown; each group's `order` is set to its position in the array. Groups you leave out of the array keep their current `order` and may end up interleaved, so send the full list.

get.description: Retrieve a single account group by id. Returns 404 if the group does not exist or belongs to another company.

name.description: The name of the account group.

archived.description: Flag indicating if the account group is archived.

order.description: A number used for ordering account groups in the UI.

put.description: Rename an account group or archive it. Archiving hides the group in the app without touching the accounts inside it.

name.description: The name of the account group.

archived.description: Flag indicating if the account group is archived.

order.description: A number used for ordering account groups in the UI.

delete.description: Delete an account group. Move every account out of the group first (`PUT /accounts/{accountId}/change_group`), otherwise the delete fails on the foreign key from accounts. To keep the grouping but hide it, archive the group with `PUT` instead.

get.description: List a company's accounts (bank, cash, credit card, loan, transit, other) with the integration managing each one, where there is one. `includeInCashBalance` decides whether an account counts towards the cash position, so a loan or a holding account can be excluded from it. Archived accounts are included; filter on `archived` for the live ones. Transaction counts and last-transaction dates only appear for callers with `transactions:read`.

type.description: The type of account: bank, cash, creditCard, loan, other, or transit (system-managed, holds the in-flight bookings of transfers between accounts).

name.description: The name of the account.

accountNumber.description: The bank account number. Null if not provided.

includeInCashBalance.description: Whether this account should be included in cash balance calculations and cash flow reports.

accountGroupId.description: The ID of the account group this account belongs to. Null if not part of any group.

archived.description: Flag indicating if the account is archived and should be hidden from most views.

order.description: A number used for ordering accounts in the UI.

balanceMismatchReportedBalances.description: The balances reported by the bank in the last failed balance consistency check. Can contain multiple values, e.g. balance with and without pending transactions. Present while automated imports keep failing the check, so also while status is still 'active'.

balanceMismatchCalculatedBalance.description: The balance derived from summing all transactions in the last failed balance consistency check. Present while automated imports keep failing the check, so also while status is still 'active'.

balanceMismatchSince.description: The ISO datetime since when automated imports have consecutively failed the balance consistency check. Used to confirm a mismatch before it is surfaced, so it can be present while status is still 'active'. Cleared by the next successful import. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

balanceMismatchNotifiedTime.description: The ISO datetime when the owners were last notified about the current balance mismatch, by the first notice or a reminder. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

balanceMismatchReminderCount.description: How many reminders about the current balance mismatch were sent after the first notice.

direction.description: Which way the period runs from the transaction date. `forward` (the default) starts on the transaction date; `backward` ends on it. Example: 3 months backward from 2026-09-14 covers 2026-06-15 to 2026-09-14.

offset.description: How many periods to shift the start away from the period containing the transaction date. 0 is the period of the transaction, -1 the one before, 1 the one after.

interval.description: How many consecutive periods the range spans, starting at the shifted period. Defaults to 1. Example: `month`, offset -3, interval 3 covers the three full calendar months before the transaction month.

usingDateRule.description: The default date rule to apply to transactions from this counterparty.

revenue.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered revenue in percent.

cogs.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered cost of goods sold in percent.

cac.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered customer acquisition cost in percent.

pd.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered product development in percent.

ga.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered general and administrative in percent.

no.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered non-operating expenses in percent.

neutral.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered neutral in percent.

plSplit.description: The default split of the transaction amount into different Profit & Loss (P&L) types. The sum of the percentages needs to be 100%.

passThroughTax.description: The pass-through tax (e.g. VAT) that comes on top of the amount covered by the P&L split.

transferTargetAccountId.description: Only valid when the default category is the system transfer category. template.description: Categorization template applied to every wallet payment line under this cost center. Null means skipped. `passThroughTax` and `usingDateRule` are placeholders for Finway — real tax / dates come from the Antrag line.

label.description: Human-readable Kostenstelle label as last seen in Finway (e.g. 'Materialkosten/ Produktion'). Refreshed on every Antrag upload.

mappedTime.description: ISO datetime the mapping was created.

mappedByUserId.description: Firebase UID that created the mapping.

costCategoryMap.description: Map keyed by Finway CostCenter1ID (e.g. '30') to the chosen SaaSFlow category. Always present in Antrag exports, stable across Finway tenants — preferred over Sachkonto string keying.

finwayWebUrl.description: The customer's Finway web address (https://<name>.finway.de) the sync logs in to. Null when the integration only takes uploads.

finwayApiUrl.description: The Finway API address read from the web app at connect time (https://api.<deployment>.finway.de/api).

finwayLoginEmail.description: Email of the read-only Finway user the sync logs in as, for display.

finwayCompanyId.description: Finway's id of the company the login opens. A later login has to open the same one, so two Finway wallets never mix in one account.

syncActorUserId.description: SaaSFlow user who connected the Finway login. Scheduled syncs record their imports under this user.

lastAccountSyncTime.description: When the last sync finished without an error. Null before the first one.

lastSyncError.description: The error of the last sync. Null when it worked.

outcome.description: imported: rows were added or updated. unchanged: same file as last time. needsReview: importing would remove rows that carry manual edits, so the sync left the month alone. failed: the file could not be read.

inserted.description: For imported: payments the statement added that SaaSFlow did not have yet.

updated.description: For imported: payments the statement changed, such as a corrected amount or vendor. Payments imported ahead of the statement that it now confirms are not counted.

removed.description: For imported: payments SaaSFlow had for the month that the statement no longer lists.

months.description: One entry per wallet statement month the sync looked at.

antragsImported.description: Final Anträge the expense import processed.

transactionsCategorized.description: Wallet payments that got new or changed categorizations.

deferredAntragCount.description: Anträge left for later because a cost center has no mapping yet.

unmappedCostCenters.description: Cost centers waiting for a mapping.

antragsSkippedBeforeDataStart.description: Anträge left out because no wallet payment from the data start date on points to them.

outcome.description: 'seeded': the sync set the opening balance. 'matches': the account ends on Finway's balance. 'differs': an opening balance set earlier does not lead to Finway's balance. 'notReconciled': no opening balance yet, and the imported payments do not add up to Finway's balance.

date.description: Day of the opening balance: the day before the first transaction SaaSFlow keeps.

value.description: Balance at the end of that day, as set or as Finway shows it.

expected.description: For 'differs': the opening balance that would lead to Finway's balance.

asOf.description: Month ('YYYY-MM') of the Finway statement compared against.

openingBalance.description: How the account compares with Finway. Null when the sync could not check it, for example while a month waits for review.

from.description: First day without a wallet statement: the day after the last statement month, or the data start date when that is later.

rows.description: Wallet payments and top-ups from that day on, imported from Finway ahead of their statement.

removed.description: Provisional rows removed because Finway reports the payment as failed.

error.description: What this run could not import or update, or null: the transaction list failing, payments in another currency, or edited payments Finway changed since.

ongoing.description: Payments of months Finway has no statement for yet (normally the ongoing month), imported from Finway's transaction list. The month's statement takes them over once Finway issues it.

lastSyncSummary.description: What the last sync did, for the sync dialog.

sha256.description: Hash of the statement CSV the sync imported.

syncedStatements.description: Wallet statements the sync imported, keyed by month ('YYYY-MM'). A statement whose file is unchanged is not imported again.

notifiedUnmappedCostCenterIds.description: Cost centers (CostCenter1ID) without a mapping that the team already knows about, from a notification or from the Sync now dialog, so a sync that runs several times a day tells them once. A cost center leaves the list once it no longer waits.

syncLeaseUntil.description: Set while a sync runs, so a second one does not start: Finway allows one session per user, and a second login would end the first.

userId.description: The subscriber ID (Teilnehmer-ID) the bank assigned.

accountHolder.description: The account holder's legal name, as the bank knows it. Printed on the initialisation letter. Null or missing for connections set up before it was asked for; the letter then uses the name in the certificates.

setupStep.description: How far the setup has come. `sendKeys`: the keys are not yet with the bank. `awaitActivation`: the keys are sent and the bank still has to activate them after receiving the signed letter. `confirmBankKeys`: the bank's keys were fetched and the customer has to compare them with the bank's letter (also after the bank changed its keys). `selectAccounts`: the customer picks the accounts to import. `ready`: statements are imported.

iniSentTime.description: When the bank accepted the signature key (INI). Banks refuse a second INI, so a retry after a failed HIA skips it. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

keysSentTime.description: When the bank accepted the keys (INI and HIA). Null before. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

activationCheckedTime.description: When SaaSFlow last asked the bank whether it activated the keys. Null before the first check. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

authenticationFingerprint.description: SHA-256 hash of the bank's authentication key (X002), as printed in the bank's letter.

encryptionFingerprint.description: SHA-256 hash of the bank's encryption key (E002), as printed in the bank's letter.

fetchedTime.description: When the keys were fetched from the bank. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

confirmedTime.description: When the customer confirmed that the hashes match the bank's letter. Null until then; no statements are downloaded before. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

bankKeys.description: The bank's keys the customer confirmed. Null until the customer confirmed them once.

authenticationFingerprint.description: SHA-256 hash of the bank's authentication key (X002), as printed in the bank's letter.

encryptionFingerprint.description: SHA-256 hash of the bank's encryption key (E002), as printed in the bank's letter.

fetchedTime.description: When the keys were fetched from the bank. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

pendingBankKeys.description: Bank keys fetched but not yet confirmed: after the bank activated the connection, or after it changed its keys. Null when there are none.

iban.description: The IBAN, as the bank reports it.

currency.description: The account currency (ISO 4217). Null when the bank does not report it.

holder.description: The account holder. Null when the bank does not report it.

bankAccounts.description: The accounts the bank lets this subscriber read. Null when the bank does not report them; then every account that shows up in a statement is imported.

accountsListedTime.description: When the bank last answered the request for the account list, or said it does not offer one. Null before. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

selectedIbans.description: The IBANs the customer chose to import. Null imports every account the statements contain.

accountsSelectedTime.description: When the customer chose the accounts to import. Null before. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

canUpload.description: Whether the bank lets this subscriber upload orders, such as payment files. SaaSFlow only downloads. Null when the bank does not report permissions.

canAuthorisePayments.description: Whether the subscriber's uploads may authorise payments: signature class E, A or B, or an upload permission whose class is unknown. A transport signature (class T) does not: it permits transport submission but does not provide a bank-technical authorising signature. Setup refuses a subscriber that may authorise payments. Null when the bank does not report permissions; missing for connections whose accounts were listed before this was checked.

historyCursor.description: Where the first import walks back from next: statements before this date are still to be asked for. Null once the walk is done or before it starts. Format: YYYY-MM-DD

historyStartDate.description: The oldest statement date the bank delivered during the first import. Null before the first import. Format: YYYY-MM-DD

lastAccountSyncTime.description: When the last successful sync finished. Null before the first one. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

lastSyncError.description: The error reported by the last failed sync or setup step. Null when it worked.

finApiInstitutionId.description: The bank's entry in the finAPI bank catalog, used only for its logo; the connection does not go through finAPI. Set when every imported account resolves to the same entry, null otherwise; missing before the first sync looked it up.

integration.description: The integration managing this account (null for manual accounts or when the bank connection has no integrationId).

post.description: Create an account. Use `importType: "manual"` for one you will fill by hand or by CSV; accounts fed by a bank connection are created by the integration itself. `includeInCashBalance` decides whether it counts towards the cash position, which is usually false for loans. Pass `initialBalance` to seed the opening balance so the running balance is right from day one, dated before any transaction you then import. `order` is required and sets its position in the list.

archived.description: Flag indicating if the account is archived and should be hidden from most views.

expectedAnnualReturn.description: The expected annual return percentage for this account, if applicable.

get.description: Get the balance of each account at two points in time and the change between them. Keyed by account id, `value` is the balance on `endDate` and `valuePreviousPeriod` the balance on `startDate`. Amounts are in each account's own currency, named in `defaultCurrency`, so do not sum across accounts without converting first. Narrow to specific accounts with a comma-separated `accountIds`. For a converted series over time rather than two snapshots, use `daily_balance`.

get.description: Get the day-by-day cumulative balance across accounts, returned as `[date, balance]` tuples. Unlike the per-account balances endpoint, these are converted into the company's base currency and summed, so this is the series to plot as a cash curve. Restrict it to specific accounts with a comma-separated `accountIds`.

post.description: Preview what cutting off history before a date would do, without changing anything. Returns per-account transaction counts and date ranges, plus `suggestedDate`: the earliest date from which every account has data, which is the point where the books stop having gaps. Loan accounts are ignored when computing it, since their data only spans payout to final repayment and a late loan is not a coverage gap. Only accounts with transactions are listed, and transit accounts are left out. Always run this before `remove_history`.

200.description: Per-account history stats for the remove-history flow. Only accounts that have transactions appear; transit accounts are excluded. suggestedDate is the first date on which every listed account has data, ignoring loan accounts (their data only spans payout to final repayment, so a late loan is not a coverage gap).

post.description: Permanently delete transactions before `beforeDate` on the listed accounts and set the company data start date, so reporting begins from a clean, fully covered period. Each collapsed account gets an initial-balance seed so its running balance still ends up right; supply `initialBalances` for accounts with no existing seed, such as CSV wallets whose uploads started late, otherwise the seed is derived from the recorded sum. Pass an empty `accountIds` to only move the data start date. Accounts left with no transactions are archived and returned in `archivedAccountIds`. Transit accounts are refused with 422. This cannot be undone, so preview first.

200.description: History removed for the selected accounts and the company data start date set. An empty accountIds list only sets the date.

404.description: One of the accounts was not found

422.description: A transit account cannot have its history removed directly

put.description: Reorder accounts inside one group, and move them into it in the same call. Every id in `accountIds` is assigned to `accountGroupId` (null for the ungrouped list) and given an `order` matching its position, so send the full contents of the target group rather than just the account that moved. Fails with 404 if the group does not exist.

categoryId.description: The default category to assign to transactions from this counterparty.

direction.description: Which way the period runs from the transaction date. `forward` (the default) starts on the transaction date; `backward` ends on it. Example: 3 months backward from 2026-09-14 covers 2026-06-15 to 2026-09-14.

offset.description: How many periods to shift the start away from the period containing the transaction date. 0 is the period of the transaction, -1 the one before, 1 the one after.

interval.description: How many consecutive periods the range spans, starting at the shifted period. Defaults to 1. Example: `month`, offset -3, interval 3 covers the three full calendar months before the transaction month.

usingDateRule.description: The default date rule to apply to transactions from this counterparty.

revenue.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered revenue in percent.

cogs.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered cost of goods sold in percent.

cac.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered customer acquisition cost in percent.

pd.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered product development in percent.

ga.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered general and administrative in percent.

no.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered non-operating expenses in percent.

neutral.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered neutral in percent.

plSplit.description: The default split of the transaction amount into different Profit & Loss (P&L) types. The sum of the percentages needs to be 100%.

passThroughTax.description: The pass-through tax (e.g. VAT) that comes on top of the amount covered by the P&L split.

transferTargetAccountId.description: Only valid when the default category is the system transfer category. The account that receives the counter transaction so each applied transfer is booked closed instead of left as an open leg. Must be an active, non-transit account of the same company that accepts manual transactions. Omit or null to leave transfers open.

template.description: Categorization template applied to every wallet payment line under this cost center. Null means skipped. `passThroughTax` and `usingDateRule` are placeholders for Finway — real tax / dates come from the Antrag line.

label.description: Human-readable Kostenstelle label as last seen in Finway (e.g. 'Materialkosten/ Produktion'). Refreshed on every Antrag upload.

mappedTime.description: ISO datetime the mapping was created.

mappedByUserId.description: Firebase UID that created the mapping.

costCategoryMap.description: Map keyed by Finway CostCenter1ID (e.g. '30') to the chosen SaaSFlow category. Always present in Antrag exports, stable across Finway tenants — preferred over Sachkonto string keying.

finwayWebUrl.description: The customer's Finway web address (https://<name>.finway.de) the sync logs in to. Null when the integration only takes uploads.

finwayApiUrl.description: The Finway API address read from the web app at connect time (https://api.<deployment>.finway.de/api).

finwayLoginEmail.description: Email of the read-only Finway user the sync logs in as, for display.

finwayCompanyId.description: Finway's id of the company the login opens. A later login has to open the same one, so two Finway wallets never mix in one account.

syncActorUserId.description: SaaSFlow user who connected the Finway login. Scheduled syncs record their imports under this user.

lastAccountSyncTime.description: When the last sync finished without an error. Null before the first one.

lastSyncError.description: The error of the last sync. Null when it worked.

outcome.description: imported: rows were added or updated. unchanged: same file as last time. needsReview: importing would remove rows that carry manual edits, so the sync left the month alone. failed: the file could not be read.

inserted.description: For imported: payments the statement added that SaaSFlow did not have yet.

updated.description: For imported: payments the statement changed, such as a corrected amount or vendor. Payments imported ahead of the statement that it now confirms are not counted.

removed.description: For imported: payments SaaSFlow had for the month that the statement no longer lists.

months.description: One entry per wallet statement month the sync looked at.

antragsImported.description: Final Anträge the expense import processed.

transactionsCategorized.description: Wallet payments that got new or changed categorizations.

deferredAntragCount.description: Anträge left for later because a cost center has no mapping yet.

unmappedCostCenters.description: Cost centers waiting for a mapping.

antragsSkippedBeforeDataStart.description: Anträge left out because no wallet payment from the data start date on points to them.

outcome.description: 'seeded': the sync set the opening balance. 'matches': the account ends on Finway's balance. 'differs': an opening balance set earlier does not lead to Finway's balance. 'notReconciled': no opening balance yet, and the imported payments do not add up to Finway's balance.

date.description: Day of the opening balance: the day before the first transaction SaaSFlow keeps.

value.description: Balance at the end of that day, as set or as Finway shows it.

expected.description: For 'differs': the opening balance that would lead to Finway's balance.

asOf.description: Month ('YYYY-MM') of the Finway statement compared against.

openingBalance.description: How the account compares with Finway. Null when the sync could not check it, for example while a month waits for review.

from.description: First day without a wallet statement: the day after the last statement month, or the data start date when that is later.

rows.description: Wallet payments and top-ups from that day on, imported from Finway ahead of their statement.

removed.description: Provisional rows removed because Finway reports the payment as failed.

error.description: What this run could not import or update, or null: the transaction list failing, payments in another currency, or edited payments Finway changed since.

ongoing.description: Payments of months Finway has no statement for yet (normally the ongoing month), imported from Finway's transaction list. The month's statement takes them over once Finway issues it.

lastSyncSummary.description: What the last sync did, for the sync dialog.

sha256.description: Hash of the statement CSV the sync imported.

syncedStatements.description: Wallet statements the sync imported, keyed by month ('YYYY-MM'). A statement whose file is unchanged is not imported again.

notifiedUnmappedCostCenterIds.description: Cost centers (CostCenter1ID) without a mapping that the team already knows about, from a notification or from the Sync now dialog, so a sync that runs several times a day tells them once. A cost center leaves the list once it no longer waits.

syncLeaseUntil.description: Set while a sync runs, so a second one does not start: Finway allows one session per user, and a second login would end the first.

accountHolder.description: The account holder's legal name, as the bank knows it. Printed on the initialisation letter. Null or missing for connections set up before it was asked for; the letter then uses the name in the certificates.

setupStep.description: How far the setup has come. `sendKeys`: the keys are not yet with the bank. `awaitActivation`: the keys are sent and the bank still has to activate them after receiving the signed letter. `confirmBankKeys`: the bank's keys were fetched and the customer has to compare them with the bank's letter (also after the bank changed its keys). `selectAccounts`: the customer picks the accounts to import. `ready`: statements are imported.

iniSentTime.description: When the bank accepted the signature key (INI). Banks refuse a second INI, so a retry after a failed HIA skips it. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

keysSentTime.description: When the bank accepted the keys (INI and HIA). Null before. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

activationCheckedTime.description: When SaaSFlow last asked the bank whether it activated the keys. Null before the first check. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

authenticationFingerprint.description: SHA-256 hash of the bank's authentication key (X002), as printed in the bank's letter.

encryptionFingerprint.description: SHA-256 hash of the bank's encryption key (E002), as printed in the bank's letter.

fetchedTime.description: When the keys were fetched from the bank. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

409.description: An active transit account for this currency already exists — archive it first

422.description: Transit accounts cannot change their type or currency

delete.description: Delete an account and cascade-delete every transaction on it, along with their categorizations. That rewrites cash balances and the P&L for every period the account covered, so archive it instead when the intent is only to get it off the screen. Transfers in other accounts that were linked to it lose their link and show as open again; `GET /accounts/{accountId}/delete_preview` counts them beforehand.

get.description: Preview what deleting an account would do to transfers in other accounts, without changing anything. Deleting an account removes its transactions, and a transfer in another account whose counterpart sat on it loses its link and shows as open again. That holds for direct links and for transfers routed through a transit account, whose transit bookings are removed as well. A counter transaction SaaSFlow created automatically for one of this account's transfers is deleted instead. Call this before `DELETE /accounts/{accountId}` to tell the user which accounts are affected.

200.description: The transfers in other accounts the delete would reopen or remove

reopenedTransferCount.description: Transactions on that account that stay but lose their transfer link and show as open again.

removedCounterCount.description: Counter transactions SaaSFlow created automatically on that account for transfers of this account. They are deleted too.

otherAccounts.description: Per other account, the transfers linked to this account, directly or through a transit account. Transit accounts are left out. Empty when nothing elsewhere is linked.

put.description: Archive an account. It drops out of the app's account lists and pickers while its transactions and history stay intact, which is the right move for a closed bank account. Reversible with `/unarchive`.

balanceMismatchReportedBalances.description: The balances reported by the bank in the last failed balance consistency check. balanceMismatchReminderCount.description: How many reminders about the current balance mismatch were sent after the first notice.

get.description: List a company's transaction categories. Each category declares the P&L lines it can post to through `plTypes` (revenue, cogs, cac, pd, ga, no, neutral), which is what lets one category split across the P&L. `used` counts everything currently assigned to the category, both transactions and planned transactions, so a zero there means the category can be deleted outright; `usedTransactions` and `usedPlannedTransactions` break that total down. Categories flagged `system` are created and maintained by SaaSFlow and cannot be deleted at all.

used.description: Total number of things currently assigned to this category: transactions plus planned transactions. Zero means the category can be deleted outright.

delete.description: Delete a category. Refused with 409 while any transaction is still categorized under it or any planned transaction still uses it, and with 400 for system categories, which SaaSFlow manages. To retire a category that is in use, merge it into another one instead.

409.description: Category is in use by transactions

post.description: Delete several categories at once. All or nothing: if any id in the list is a system category, or still has transactions or planned transactions attached, nothing is deleted and the call fails with 400 or 409.

409.description: A selected category is in use by transactions or planned transactions

post.description: Merge several categories into one, in a single transaction. Creates the category described by `newCategory`, then repoints everything that referenced the old ids: transaction categorizations, the default categorization on customers and vendors, and the default category on accounts. The old categories are deleted afterwards. This is how to retire duplicates without stranding history, since a plain delete is refused while transactions still use the category. One thing to know before running it: plan items on the old categories are deleted rather than repointed, so a merge drops that part of the financial plan. Returns the new category.

get.description: List customers, each enriched with its transaction count (`nrTransactions`), the date of its latest settled transaction (`lastTransactionDate`, null when there is none), subscription count, and current committed MRR. The response shape depends on `limit`: send it and you get `{ items, totalCount }`, omit it and you get a bare array of every customer. `q` matches on name, or exactly on an external id the customer carries (a Stripe customer id, a Digistore24 buyer id), `onlyActive=true` keeps just the customers whose current cMRR is above zero, `linkedTo` keeps the customers linked to an integration (`stripe`, `hubspot`, `digistore24`, …, `any`, or `none`), `productId` keeps the customers with a subscription that booked an event against that product, and `unused=true` keeps the customers with no transaction, no subscription and no planned transaction. Rows come sorted by name unless `sortBy=currentCMRR` asks for the cMRR order (converted to the base currency for comparing, customers without cMRR last in both directions), which needs `subscriptions:read` and falls back to name order without it. The enrichment fields are gated separately from customer master data, so a caller without `transactions:read` or `subscriptions:read` gets those keys omitted rather than nulled.

delete.description: Delete a customer. This reaches further than it looks: their subscriptions are cascade-deleted, which changes MRR history, and any planned transaction pointing at them is unassigned. Transactions survive but lose their counterparty, and each one is flagged to stay out of auto-categorization so the deleted customer is not immediately re-matched. For a duplicate record, merge instead of deleting.

post.description: Delete many customers in one call. `selection` works two ways: `mode: "ids"` with an explicit list, or `mode: "filter"` with the same filter the list endpoint takes (`q`, `onlyActive`, `linkedTo`, `productId`, `unused`) plus `excludedIds` for the rows the user unticked. Filter mode is what "select all matching" in the UI sends, so nothing has to round-trip every id. Selections resolving to more than 10,000 customers are refused with 413 and a body giving the count and the cap. The response reports how many rows were actually affected.

post.description: Merge duplicate customers into one, in a single transaction. Creates the customer described by `newCustomer`, repoints the transaction categorizations, subscriptions, and external ids of every id in `customerIds` onto it, then deletes the originals. Use this rather than delete when the same account was imported twice: it keeps revenue history and MRR continuous, where a delete would cascade the subscriptions away. Returns the merged customer with its `logoUrl` and combined `externalIds`.

post.description: Book one or more Stripe invoices onto the transaction that paid them, taking the service period, tax split and customer from each invoice instead of the payment date. Pass several ids when one transfer settled several invoices. Re-linking an invoice replaces only the categorizations it produced, so anything categorized by hand is kept. If the payer settled for a different amount than was invoiced, the difference is left uncategorized and the transaction stays open, because only the customer knows what the difference was.

categorizationTemplate.description: Apply a categorization template to every selected transaction. The split is computed per-row from each row`s amount and date. post.description: Given up to 10,000 transaction ids, return which of them are still open and the amount of each. Built for review tooling that produced suggestions a while ago and needs to know what is still worth applying before showing it. "Open" is broader than uncategorized: it also covers rows whose categorizations do not sum to the amount, and incomplete transfers. `amountsById` covers every id that exists in this company, so a cluster total can be computed here rather than trusted from the caller.

200.description: The subset of the given transactions that are still open.

post.description: Bulk-import transactions, which is the endpoint behind CSV upload and any backfill of history. Amounts follow the same convention as single creation: signed decimal strings, negative for money out. Transit accounts are system-managed and cannot be imported into (422). Rows dated before the company data start date are not imported; `skippedBeforeDataStart` says how many, and `dataStartDate` which date applied. Only counts come back, so keep your own idempotency key if the import may be retried.

post.description: Break a transfer link. How much comes apart depends on `link`: `path` dissolves the whole transfer and removes the transit bookings SaaSFlow created, `counter` (the default) detaches only this transaction from its transit booking, and `transit` reopens a closed path by unlinking the two transit positions. For a directly linked transfer with no transit hop, `link` is ignored. A 409 means someone else changed the link first, so reload and retry rather than forcing it.

link.description: How much of a transit-routed transfer to unlink: "path" dissolves the whole transfer — both account transactions are unlinked and the auto-created transit bookings are removed; "counter" (default) unlinks only this transaction from its transit booking; "transit" reopens a closed path by unlinking only the two transit positions. For directly linked (non-transit) transfers the value is ignored.

409.description: The link changed concurrently — reload and retry

422.description: The transfer cannot be unlinked in this state

post.description: Book the missing other half of a transfer. When money left one account and the matching arrival was never imported, for example on a cash or wallet account nobody feeds, this creates the opposing transaction on `targetAccountId` and links the two. Use `link_transfer` instead when both sides already exist. Returns 409 if the source is already linked or was changed concurrently.

post.description: Link two existing transactions as the two legs of one transfer, so the movement stops counting as income on one side and spend on the other. Pass the source transaction with the categorization that represents the transfer, plus the target transaction. Legs that cannot be matched directly, across currencies or dates, are routed through a transit account, which is why the resulting chain can have more than two nodes. Returns 409 if either side is already linked or changed concurrently, and 422 when the two cannot form a transfer at all.

get.description: List a company's connected integrations: payment and billing providers, CRMs, and accounting and expense tools. Each entry carries the provider, its connection state, and the sync metadata the app shows on the integrations screen. `initialSetupComplete` false means the first import is still running; `status` `error` means the connection broke and the person has to reconnect it (`integrations_connect_link` with the `integrationId`). Bank connections are not listed here: they are accounts (`accounts_list`). To connect a new provider, use `integrations_connect_link`.

categoryId.description: The default category to assign to transactions from this counterparty.

direction.description: Which way the period runs from the transaction date. `forward` (the default) starts on the transaction date; `backward` ends on it. Example: 3 months backward from 2026-09-14 covers 2026-06-15 to 2026-09-14.

offset.description: How many periods to shift the start away from the period containing the transaction date. 0 is the period of the transaction, -1 the one before, 1 the one after.

interval.description: How many consecutive periods the range spans, starting at the shifted period. Defaults to 1. Example: `month`, offset -3, interval 3 covers the three full calendar months before the transaction month.

usingDateRule.description: The default date rule to apply to transactions from this counterparty.

revenue.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered revenue in percent.

cogs.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered cost of goods sold in percent.

cac.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered customer acquisition cost in percent.

pd.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered product development in percent.

ga.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered general and administrative in percent.

no.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered non-operating expenses in percent.

neutral.description: The share of the transaction amount that is considered neutral in percent.

plSplit.description: The default split of the transaction amount into different Profit & Loss (P&L) types. The sum of the percentages needs to be 100%.

passThroughTax.description: The pass-through tax (e.g. VAT) that comes on top of the amount covered by the P&L split.

transferTargetAccountId.description: Only valid when the default category is the system transfer category. The account that receives the counter transaction so each applied transfer is booked closed instead of left as an open leg. Must be an active, non-transit account of the same company that accepts manual transactions. Omit or null to leave transfers open.

template.description: Categorization template applied to every wallet payment line under this cost center. Null means skipped. `passThroughTax` and `usingDateRule` are placeholders for Finway — real tax / dates come from the Antrag line.

label.description: Human-readable Kostenstelle label as last seen in Finway (e.g. 'Materialkosten/ Produktion'). Refreshed on every Antrag upload.

mappedTime.description: ISO datetime the mapping was created.

mappedByUserId.description: Firebase UID that created the mapping.

costCategoryMap.description: Map keyed by Finway CostCenter1ID (e.g. '30') to the chosen SaaSFlow category. Always present in Antrag exports, stable across Finway tenants — preferred over Sachkonto string keying.

finwayWebUrl.description: The customer's Finway web address (https://<name>.finway.de) the sync logs in to. Null when the integration only takes uploads.

finwayApiUrl.description: The Finway API address read from the web app at connect time (https://api.<deployment>.finway.de/api).

finwayLoginEmail.description: Email of the read-only Finway user the sync logs in as, for display.

finwayCompanyId.description: Finway's id of the company the login opens. A later login has to open the same one, so two Finway wallets never mix in one account.

syncActorUserId.description: SaaSFlow user who connected the Finway login. Scheduled syncs record their imports under this user.

lastAccountSyncTime.description: When the last sync finished without an error. Null before the first one.

lastSyncError.description: The error of the last sync. Null when it worked.

outcome.description: imported: rows were added or updated. unchanged: same file as last time. needsReview: importing would remove rows that carry manual edits, so the sync left the month alone. failed: the file could not be read.

inserted.description: For imported: payments the statement added that SaaSFlow did not have yet.

updated.description: For imported: payments the statement changed, such as a corrected amount or vendor. Payments imported ahead of the statement that it now confirms are not counted.

removed.description: For imported: payments SaaSFlow had for the month that the statement no longer lists.

months.description: One entry per wallet statement month the sync looked at.

antragsImported.description: Final Anträge the expense import processed.

transactionsCategorized.description: Wallet payments that got new or changed categorizations.

deferredAntragCount.description: Anträge left for later because a cost center has no mapping yet.

unmappedCostCenters.description: Cost centers waiting for a mapping.

antragsSkippedBeforeDataStart.description: Anträge left out because no wallet payment from the data start date on points to them.

outcome.description: 'seeded': the sync set the opening balance. 'matches': the account ends on Finway's balance. 'differs': an opening balance set earlier does not lead to Finway's balance. 'notReconciled': no opening balance yet, and the imported payments do not add up to Finway's balance.

date.description: Day of the opening balance: the day before the first transaction SaaSFlow keeps.

value.description: Balance at the end of that day, as set or as Finway shows it.

expected.description: For 'differs': the opening balance that would lead to Finway's balance.

asOf.description: Month ('YYYY-MM') of the Finway statement compared against.

openingBalance.description: How the account compares with Finway. Null when the sync could not check it, for example while a month waits for review.

from.description: First day without a wallet statement: the day after the last statement month, or the data start date when that is later.

rows.description: Wallet payments and top-ups from that day on, imported from Finway ahead of their statement.

removed.description: Provisional rows removed because Finway reports the payment as failed.

error.description: What this run could not import or update, or null: the transaction list failing, payments in another currency, or edited payments Finway changed since.

ongoing.description: Payments of months Finway has no statement for yet (normally the ongoing month), imported from Finway's transaction list. The month's statement takes them over once Finway issues it.

lastSyncSummary.description: What the last sync did, for the sync dialog.

sha256.description: Hash of the statement CSV the sync imported.

syncedStatements.description: Wallet statements the sync imported, keyed by month ('YYYY-MM'). A statement whose file is unchanged is not imported again.

notifiedUnmappedCostCenterIds.description: Cost centers (CostCenter1ID) without a mapping that the team already knows about, from a notification or from the Sync now dialog, so a sync that runs several times a day tells them once. A cost center leaves the list once it no longer waits.

syncLeaseUntil.description: Set while a sync runs, so a second one does not start: Finway allows one session per user, and a second login would end the first.

bankName.description: The name of the bank, as entered at setup.

partnerId.description: The customer ID (Kunden-ID) the bank assigned.

userId.description: The subscriber ID (Teilnehmer-ID) the bank assigned.

accountHolder.description: The account holder's legal name, as the bank knows it. Printed on the initialisation letter. Null or missing for connections set up before it was asked for; the letter then uses the name in the certificates.

setupStep.description: How far the setup has come. `sendKeys`: the keys are not yet with the bank. `awaitActivation`: the keys are sent and the bank still has to activate them after receiving the signed letter. `confirmBankKeys`: the bank's keys were fetched and the customer has to compare them with the bank's letter (also after the bank changed its keys). `selectAccounts`: the customer picks the accounts to import. `ready`: statements are imported.

iniSentTime.description: When the bank accepted the signature key (INI). Banks refuse a second INI, so a retry after a failed HIA skips it. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

keysSentTime.description: When the bank accepted the keys (INI and HIA). Null before. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

activationCheckedTime.description: When SaaSFlow last asked the bank whether it activated the keys. Null before the first check. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

authenticationFingerprint.description: SHA-256 hash of the bank's authentication key (X002), as printed in the bank's letter.

encryptionFingerprint.description: SHA-256 hash of the bank's encryption key (E002), as printed in the bank's letter.

fetchedTime.description: When the keys were fetched from the bank. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

confirmedTime.description: When the customer confirmed that the hashes match the bank's letter. Null until then; no statements are downloaded before. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

bankKeys.description: The bank's keys the customer confirmed. Null until the customer confirmed them once.

authenticationFingerprint.description: SHA-256 hash of the bank's authentication key (X002), as printed in the bank's letter.

encryptionFingerprint.description: SHA-256 hash of the bank's encryption key (E002), as printed in the bank's letter.

fetchedTime.description: When the keys were fetched from the bank. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

pendingBankKeys.description: Bank keys fetched but not yet confirmed: after the bank activated the connection, or after it changed its keys. Null when there are none.

iban.description: The IBAN, as the bank reports it.

currency.description: The account currency (ISO 4217). Null when the bank does not report it.

holder.description: The account holder. Null when the bank does not report it.

bankAccounts.description: The accounts the bank lets this subscriber read. Null when the bank does not report them; then every account that shows up in a statement is imported.

accountsListedTime.description: When the bank last answered the request for the account list, or said it does not offer one. Null before. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

selectedIbans.description: The IBANs the customer chose to import. Null imports every account the statements contain.

accountsSelectedTime.description: When the customer chose the accounts to import. Null before. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

canUpload.description: Whether the bank lets this subscriber upload orders, such as payment files. SaaSFlow only downloads. Null when the bank does not report permissions.

canAuthorisePayments.description: Whether the subscriber's uploads may authorise payments: signature class E, A or B, or an upload permission whose class is unknown. A transport signature (class T) does not: it permits transport submission but does not provide a bank-technical authorising signature. Setup refuses a subscriber that may authorise payments. Null when the bank does not report permissions; missing for connections whose accounts were listed before this was checked.

historyCursor.description: Where the first import walks back from next: statements before this date are still to be asked for. Null once the walk is done or before it starts. Format: YYYY-MM-DD

historyStartDate.description: The oldest statement date the bank delivered during the first import. Null before the first import. Format: YYYY-MM-DD

lastAccountSyncTime.description: When the last successful sync finished. Null before the first one. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ

lastSyncError.description: The error reported by the last failed sync or setup step. Null when it worked.

finApiInstitutionId.description: The bank's entry in the finAPI bank catalog, used only for its logo; the connection does not go through finAPI. Set when every imported account resolves to the same entry, null otherwise; missing before the first sync looked it up.

costCategoryMap.description: Map keyed by Finway CostCenter1ID (e.g. '30') to the chosen SaaSFlow category. Always present in Antrag exports, stable across Finway tenants — preferred over Sachkonto string keying.

finwayWebUrl.description: The customer's Finway web address (https://<name>.finway.de) the sync logs in to. Null when the integration only takes uploads.

finwayApiUrl.description: The Finway API address read from the web app at connect time (https://api.<deployment>.finway.de/api).

finwayLoginEmail.description: Email of the read-only Finway user the sync logs in as, for display.

finwayCompanyId.description: Finway's id of the company the login opens. A later login has to open the same one, so two Finway wallets never mix in one account.

syncActorUserId.description: SaaSFlow user who connected the Finway login. Scheduled syncs record their imports under this user.

lastAccountSyncTime.description: When the last sync finished without an error. Null before the first one.

lastSyncError.description: The error of the last sync. Null when it worked.

outcome.description: imported: rows were added or updated. unchanged: same file as last time. needsReview: importing would remove rows that carry manual edits, so the sync left the month alone. failed: the file could not be read.

inserted.description: For imported: payments the statement added that SaaSFlow did not have yet.

updated.description: For imported: payments the statement changed, such as a corrected amount or vendor. Payments imported ahead of the statement that it now confirms are not counted.

removed.description: For imported: payments SaaSFlow had for the month that the statement no longer lists.

months.description: One entry per wallet statement month the sync looked at.

antragsImported.description: Final Anträge the expense import processed.

transactionsCategorized.description: Wallet payments that got new or changed categorizations.

deferredAntragCount.description: Anträge left for later because a cost center has no mapping yet.

unmappedCostCenters.description: Cost centers waiting for a mapping.

antragsSkippedBeforeDataStart.description: Anträge left out because no wallet payment from the data start date on points to them.

outcome.description: 'seeded': the sync set the opening balance. 'matches': the account ends on Finway's balance. 'differs': an opening balance set earlier does not lead to Finway's balance. 'notReconciled': no opening balance yet, and the imported payments do not add up to Finway's balance.

date.description: Day of the opening balance: the day before the first transaction SaaSFlow keeps.

value.description: Balance at the end of that day, as set or as Finway shows it.

expected.description: For 'differs': the opening balance that would lead to Finway's balance.

asOf.description: Month ('YYYY-MM') of the Finway statement compared against.

openingBalance.description: How the account compares with Finway. Null when the sync could not check it, for example while a month waits for review.

from.description: First day without a wallet statement: the day after the last statement month, or the data start date when that is later.

rows.description: Wallet payments and top-ups from that day on, imported from Finway ahead of their statement.

removed.description: Provisional rows removed because Finway reports the payment as failed.

error.description: What this run could not import or update, or null: the transaction list failing, payments in another currency, or edited payments Finway changed since.

ongoing.description: Payments of months Finway has no statement for yet (normally the ongoing month), imported from Finway's transaction list. The month's statement takes them over once Finway issues it.

lastSyncSummary.description: What the last sync did, for the sync dialog.

sha256.description: Hash of the statement CSV the sync imported.

syncedStatements.description: Wallet statements the sync imported, keyed by month ('YYYY-MM'). A statement whose file is unchanged is not imported again.

notifiedUnmappedCostCenterIds.description: Cost centers (CostCenter1ID) without a mapping that the team already knows about, from a notification or from the Sync now dialog, so a sync that runs several times a day tells them once. A cost center leaves the list once it no longer waits.

syncLeaseUntil.description: Set while a sync runs, so a second one does not start: Finway allows one session per user, and a second login would end the first.

delete.description: Disconnect an integration. By default (`convertToManual=true`) the accounts it managed are kept along with their transaction history and switched to manual, so nothing disappears from the books. Pass `convertToManual=false` only when the accounts and their data should go too.

get.description: Get a link that opens the connect dialog for one provider in the SaaSFlow app, for the person to finish: they sign in with the provider there (Stripe, HubSpot, Salesforce, Slack, Digistore24) or upload its export (Pleo, Finway, DATEV payroll; with the file in hand, `integrations_upload` does that without the person). `provider` `bank` opens the bank connection dialog. Pass `integrationId` instead to reconnect an integration whose `status` is `error`. Connecting needs a company role that manages integrations, which the app checks when the person opens the link. Afterwards poll `integrations_list` (banks: `accounts_list`) until the new integration shows `initialSetupComplete` true; the first import can take a few minutes.

url.description: Give this link to the person. It opens in the SaaSFlow app.

nextAction.description: What to do once the person has the link.

post.description: Pull new data from a connected provider now instead of waiting for the next scheduled sync: Stripe and Digistore24 fetch recent changes, PayPal continues its import, HubSpot refreshes subscriptions, EBICS fetches the statements the bank has ready, Finway reads its closed wallet statements and expenses when a Finway login is connected (no task id: it runs in a few minutes and records its outcome on the integration). Returns the background task id (see `background_tasks_list`); a sync already queued is not queued twice. 409 while the first import is still running. Upload-based integrations and Slack have nothing to pull (400).

409.description: First import still running

post.description: Read everything from Stripe, Digistore24, PayPal or EBICS (the last 12 months of statements) again, as the app's integration menu does. Use it when data is missing that `integrations_sync` doesn't bring back, for example after the person widened the access SaaSFlow has at the provider, or when a first import got stuck. What was imported before is updated in place, not duplicated. It runs in the background, from minutes to hours on a large account (PayPal shows `initialSetupComplete` false until it is done), and a full sync already pending is not queued twice. Needs a company role that manages integrations, and `saasflow:admin` over OAuth.

400.description: This provider has no full sync

post.description: Recompute what SaaSFlow built from a provider's data, as the repairs in the app's integration menu do. Stripe: `subscriptions` rebuilds subscriptions and their MRR, `transactions` rebuilds the transactions of the accounts Stripe feeds; both run after a fresh sync. HubSpot: `subscriptions` refreshes them from HubSpot, `categorizations` categorizes payments again from the HubSpot invoices they settle. Use it when numbers still look wrong after `integrations_sync`. Runs in the background; follow it in `background_tasks_list`. Needs a company role that manages integrations, and `saasflow:admin` over OAuth.

400.description: This provider has nothing of that kind to rebuild

409.description: First import still running

get.description: Get a link to the company's billing page in the SaaSFlow app, where the person picks a plan or changes the subscription and payment details. Choosing and paying stays with the person; only company owners can change billing. Works for a company whose plan has expired (where other routes answer `COMPANY_INACTIVE`), so the person can subscribe again.

post.description: Import a CSV export from Pleo, Finway or DATEV payroll, the way the app's upload dialog does. The first `pleoExport`, `finwayTransactions` or `datevPayroll` upload sets up the integration and its account; later ones import into it. Uploading the same file again is safe: rows are matched, not duplicated. Some uploads come back with questions for the person (see `upload.result`), and a Finway month that would change existing rows comes back as 409 with a summary until you resend with `confirmReplace`. Needs a company role that manages integrations, and a connection the person allowed to manage company settings (`saasflow:admin`).

post.description: Ask the person to approve inviting someone to the company. Once approved, SaaSFlow emails the invitation. Needs a connection the person allowed to manage company settings (`saasflow:admin`) and a company role that may make the change. Returns a `url`: give it to the person, who reviews and approves the exact change in the SaaSFlow app. Nothing changes before that. Then check `access_requests_get` for the outcome. A request expires after an hour.

role.description: The role assigned to a user within the system. Owner = full access incl. company settings, billing, and user management; editor = read/write on data; viewer = read-only. The role is also used as the default permission preset and as a non-permission marker (e.g. notifications are sent to all owners). For granular API access control, see PermissionSchema.

items.description: A granular permission in the form `<resource>:<action>`. Stored on companiesUsers and companiesApiKeys. When a grant has `permissions: null` it means unrestricted (legacy behavior derived from role).

permissions.description: An exact permission list instead of the role preset.

201.description: Waiting for the person to approve

status.description: `pending` until the person decides; `succeeded`, `failed` (see `result.error`), `rejected`, or `expired` after an hour without a decision.

url.description: Where the person reviews and approves the request.

nextAction.description: What to do with the link.

get.description: List a company's notifications, newest first, paginated. Notifications are what the app shows in its bell menu: bank connection failures, subscription changes, balance mismatches, and similar events. Without `recipientUserId`, members see their own notifications; cross-user callers can see every recipient in the company. Only notification types whose source data the caller may read are returned. Passing another user's id requires `users:manage`; without it the response is an empty page rather than a 403. Filter with `types`, and narrow subscription-change rows further with `eventType`. `totalCount` is the unpaginated total for the active filter. `earliestCreatedTime` deliberately ignores the filter so a date picker can anchor to the real start of history, and it is only computed on the first page (`offset=0`), returning null on later pages.

post.description: Create a notification about a transaction and return the created row. SaaSFlow raises most notifications itself. This endpoint only accepts the collaboration types (`assignedUser`, `bulkAssignedUser`, `taggedInComment`, `newComment`, `likedComment`), and the recipient also gets an email unless they turned that type off. `payload` must hold exactly the fields of the chosen type. Needs `transactions:write`. Addressing anyone but yourself needs `users:manage`, which API keys and OAuth apps never hold. So an OAuth app can only notify the user it acts for, and an API key, which acts for no user, cannot create notifications at all. A payload that does not match the type gets 400; missing permissions get 403.

post.description: Upload a receipt or invoice. The document goes in `fileBase64` as base64, capped at 10 MB by decoded byte length (`size` is accepted for compatibility and the stored size is derived from the bytes). PDFs and PNGs are queued for automatic parsing of amount, date, and document type; other extensions are stored as-is and never get `parseData`. post.description: Apply a reviewed batch of categorization suggestions in one call. Counterparties that do not exist yet go in `vendorsToCreate` and `customersToCreate` with a `tempId`; suggestions reference that same `tempId`, and the response maps each one to the real id it was created as. A suggestion pointing at a `tempId` that was never declared fails the whole request with 400. Creating counterparties needs `vendors:write` or `customers:write` on top of `transactions:write`. The result counts what landed and what was skipped. get.description: List individual dated occurrences of planned transactions within a date range, expanded from recurrence rules. Each item represents one expected cash event on a specific date. Amount semantics: `amount.value` is the **net** amount excluding pass-through taxes (e.g. VAT). When the underlying planned transaction has VAT, the tax portion is returned **separately** as `passThroughTaxAmount` and is **not** included in `amount.value`. To compute the total gross cash inflow / outflow for a period (e.g. for a cash flow forecast that matches what hits the bank account), sum `amount.value + (passThroughTaxAmount?.value ?? 0)` over all items. To compute net planned revenue / cost (excluding VAT, matching P&L), sum only `amount.value`. Amounts are in the currency of the planned transaction (`amount.currency`), which can differ from the account and from the company base currency, for example USD subscriptions planned on a EUR Stripe balance. Add up totals per currency, or convert before summing. Use pagination (`limit`, `offset`) to fetch all items; `totalCount` is the unpaginated total.

startDate.description: The start date of the planned transaction.

amountValue.description: The numerical value of the planned amount.

amountCurrency.description: The currency of the planned amount.

direction.description: Which way the period runs from the transaction date. `forward` (the default) starts on the transaction date; `backward` ends on it. Example: 3 months backward from 2026-09-14 covers 2026-06-15 to 2026-09-14.

offset.description: How many periods to shift the start away from the period containing the transaction date. 0 is the period of the transaction, -1 the one before, 1 the one after.

interval.description: How many consecutive periods the range spans, starting at the shifted period. Defaults to 1. Example: `month`, offset -3, interval 3 covers the three full calendar months before the transaction month.

usingDateRule.description: Rules for determining the effective/accrual date range of a transaction.

interval.description: Number of `frequency` units between occurrences.

lastDayOfMonth.description: Pin monthly occurrences to the last day of the month.

end.description: When the series stops: a last date, a number of occurrences, or null/omitted for open-ended.

source.description: The source of the planned transaction (e.g., Stripe, HubSpot).

externalInvoiceId.description: The invoice id in the source system, for issued invoices.

invoiceDate.description: The date an invoice was issued for this amount. Set only when the row represents an invoice that has been issued but not yet paid; null for predicted amounts.

serviceStartDate.description: Start of the service period the issued invoice bills for.

serviceEndDate.description: End of the service period the issued invoice bills for.

put.description: Update a planned transaction. Only the fields you send change. Edits apply to the whole rule, so changing the amount or the recurrence rewrites every future occurrence rather than just the next one, and moving `startDate` shifts the entire series. Returns 404 if it does not exist or belongs to another company.

delete.description: Delete a planned transaction and every occurrence it would have produced, past and future, which changes the cash flow forecast for all of them. To stop a recurring item from a date onward while keeping its history in the forecast, set the recurrence `end` instead.

get.description: Detect recurring spend across the whole transaction history and return the series grouped by vendor id. Recurrence is inferred from the transactions themselves, not from anything the user declared. A series needs charges at a roughly stable amount (within 1 currency unit of the first charge at that amount), one interval apart: four for weekly and monthly series, three for quarterly and longer ones. Each vendor categorization belongs to at most one series. Use this to find subscriptions a company is paying for, including ones nobody remembers signing up to. Unrelated to planned transactions, which are rules a user entered by hand.

200.description: Recurring transaction series grouped by vendor id

status.description: Whether the series is still running: `active` while its latest charge is at most one interval, plus the detection tolerance, in the past (7 + 2 days for weekly, 30 + 5 for monthly, 91 + 10 for quarterly, 182 + 14 for half-yearly, 365 + 20 for yearly). Dates are evaluated in UTC.

post.description: Run several analytics slices in one round trip. Each entry in `slices` is a descriptor `{ type, _id?, ...params }` where `type` names the slice and the rest are its parameters, the same ones the dedicated `/data/{slice}` endpoint takes. Pass `_id` to correlate each result back to its request. This is the endpoint a dashboard uses to fill many widgets at once; for a single aggregation the dedicated slice endpoint is simpler and typed. `timeZone` (IANA name, default UTC) decides where day and month boundaries fall, which changes what lands in a period. Invalid params in any slice fail the whole batch with 400, and a slice the caller lacks permission for fails it with 403. Both the invalid-params 400 and the 403 name the entry by `sliceType`, `sliceIndex` (its zero-based position in `slices`) and `sliceId` (its `_id`, when it is a string). A 400 lists every invalid entry with its validation issues in `invalidSlices`.

400.description: One or more slices have invalid params

403.description: Caller lacks permission for one of the requested slices

get.description: Free-text search across a company, grouped by entity type. Use it when you know a name but not an id: one call matches customers, vendors, and accounts on name, and transactions on counterparty or description. This backs the command palette, so each category returns at most 5 hits. Categories the caller has no read permission for come back empty rather than 403, which keeps the search box usable on partial-permission grants. When you need a full, filtered, paginated list of one entity type, use that resource's own endpoint.
